claims.text: Training a machine-learning model on existing DFT data will enable efficient prediction of melting properties for refractory materials.
The predicted properties include melting temperature, entropy of fusion, enthalpy of fusion, and volume change at the melting point.
The target refractory materials have high melting temperatures.
Machine-learning algorithms can learn relevant relationships from thermodynamic data.
Machine-learning models trained on existing DFT data will generalize to refractory materials whose melting properties are to be predicted.
The machine-learning approach can predict melting properties without expensive thermodynamic integration.
The machine-learning model will provide accurate predictions of melting properties.
Use of the machine-learning model will facilitate high-throughput calculations.
Current ab initio melting-property methods rely on expensive thermodynamic integration using ab initio molecular-dynamics simulations.
The computational expense of thermodynamic integration makes it infeasible for high-throughput calculations.
Prediction accuracy will depend on the quality of the DFT training data.
Prediction accuracy will depend on the quantity of the DFT training data.
The proposed test compares model predictions with experimental melting-property measurements for a set of refractory materials.
The hypothesis is falsified if prediction errors exceed a predefined threshold.
